en.footer: Run by volunteers and open to everyone.
en.desc_events: Regular meetings and special events of {brand}.
en.desc_join: How to join {brand}, what it costs and what to expect.
en.nf_text: We could not find that page. It may have been taken down after the event it was about.
en.events_intro: Our regular meetings and the occasional special event. The dates for the year are on the noticeboard at every meeting.
en.join_fee: Membership is {fee} a year, with a reduced rate for juniors and students. If money is a worry, tell the treasurer quietly and it will not be mentioned again.
steps: Come along to any meeting and say hello.
Try it for a month before you decide anything.
Pay the membership fee to the treasurer when you are ready.
en.news_intro: Notices from the committee and reports from recent meetings, newest first.

bundles.desc: {brand} meets every Thursday evening. Friendly games for every strength, from beginners to the club champion.
bundles.intro: We meet every Thursday to play, to analyse our games and to drink too much tea. All strengths are welcome, from first-time players to the club champion.
bundles.where: The upstairs room of the Millbrook Community Hall

why.p: Beginners sit next to old hands, and nobody minds.
No sign-up. Come when you can.
Sets and clocks are ours; tea is yours to make.

events.p: Free play, with a teaching table for beginners.
Seven rounds of fifteen minutes each. Entry is a small donation to the tea fund.
Learn the rules and a few simple openings.
The club champion plays twenty boards at once. Bring a friend and a plan.
A meal, a speech and the handing over of a very small trophy.

news.title: A new season begins
news.text: The autumn season starts next week with the club championship. New members are welcome on any night.

news.title: Thank you to everyone who came to the rapid
news.text: Twenty-six players, fourteen cups of tea per round, and a final won on the clock.

news.title: We have a new set of boards
news.text: Eight wooden boards and sets, bought with the proceeds of the summer raffle.

news.title: The junior section reopens
news.text: Children from seven years old are welcome on Tuesday afternoons, with a parent on the first visit.

join: We are a friendly club with about forty members, aged from nine to eighty-four. Most of us are not very good, and we have made our peace with that.
You do not need to own a set or know any theory. If you can move the pieces, you can play on Thursday.

faq.q: Do I need to be good?
faq.a: No. Most members are not, and the club is organised so that everybody gets a game against someone of their own strength.
Yes, on Tuesday afternoons and, with a parent, on Thursdays.

faq.q: Do you play in a league?
faq.a: We enter one team in the county league. If you want to play, tell the captain.

bundles.tagline: Walks in the hills and along the river
bundles.desc: {brand} walks every Sunday in the hills and along the river. All welcome, no experience needed.
bundles.intro: We walk every Sunday, in all weathers, at the pace of the slowest person. Come once and see; most of us began that way.

why.p: Routes of eight to twelve miles, led by people who know the paths.
A group of regulars and a steady stream of new faces.
We keep to the pace of the slowest walker.

events.p: Eight to twelve miles, with a pub stop if the weather is bad.
Three to four miles at an easy pace, ending with coffee.
Two days in the hills, with a hostel and a great deal of soup.
How to read a map, and what to do when it reads you.
We clear the river path and then walk it again, because we can.

news.title: The spring programme is out
news.text: Twelve walks between March and June, including two new routes over the ridge.

news.title: The footpath by the mill has reopened
news.text: After a year of repairs the bridge is open again. Thank you to the volunteers who gave up their Saturdays.

news.title: New walk leaders wanted
news.text: If you know a good route and can read a map, we would love to hear from you.

news.title: Thank you for the soup
news.text: The weekend away was a great success, mostly because of the soup.

join: We are a friendly group of about sixty walkers, from people who have walked all their lives to people who started last month.
You do not need special kit. Boots, a waterproof and something to drink are plenty. If in doubt, come and ask on Sunday morning.

faq.a: At the pace of the slowest person on the day, which is often the leader.
On most walks, yes, on a lead. The programme says which walks are not suitable.
We walk anyway. The pub stop is longer.

bundles.desc: {brand} rehearses on Wednesday evenings. No auditions, no need to read music, just a wish to sing.
bundles.intro: We are a choir for people who like singing and do not want to audition for it. We learn by ear, laugh a lot and sing better than we have any right to.
bundles.where: The church hall on the green

why.p: If you can hold a tune in the shower, you can hold one here.
Sopranos, altos, tenors, basses and everyone who is not sure.
One in winter and one in summer, with cake.

events.p: Warm-up, new songs and the one we still cannot get right.
Come and sing with us for the evening, with no commitment.
Carols, folk songs and one piece nobody expects.
An evening of songs in the garden of the village hall, weather permitting.
A day of workshops with a visiting conductor, lunch included.

news.title: Autumn term begins
news.text: We are learning a set of folk songs from three countries, and a round that will not stay in time.

news.title: A big thank you after the summer concert
news.text: Ninety people came, forty-one cakes were eaten, and only one verse was sung twice.

news.title: We are looking for tenors
news.text: We have plenty of sopranos and altos. If you can sing low, please come and meet us.

news.title: New music has arrived
news.text: The folders for the winter programme are in the hall. Please pencil in your marks, not pen.

join: We are about fifty singers, aged from sixteen to eighty-eight. Most of us cannot read music and have learnt songs by ear for years.
Come to any rehearsal and sing with us. We will find you a chair, a folder and someone to stand next to.

faq.a: No. There is no audition, now or later.

faq.q: Do I need to read music?
faq.a: No. We teach by ear, with the notes on paper for those who want them.

faq.q: What if I miss a week?
faq.a: Then you miss a week. Nobody will mind, and the recordings are shared online.

bundles.desc: {brand} meets monthly for talks and observing nights. Beginners and telescope owners alike are welcome.
bundles.intro: We meet once a month to hear a talk and, when the sky allows, to look through telescopes. You do not need to own a telescope, or even know where north is.
bundles.where: The library annexe, with observing on the field behind

why.p: An indoor talk, then outside if the sky is kind.
Members bring theirs, and are glad to share.
Most of us began with a pair of binoculars.

events.p: A speaker, a hot drink and usually a very good question at the end.

events.w: Clear nights near the new moon
events.p: On the field behind the library. Wrap up warmly.
Bring a telescope that will not behave and we will try to help.
We take a telescope to a local school and look at the Moon in the daytime.
A whole night under the Perseids, with flasks and deckchairs.

news.title: Autumn talks announced
news.text: Six talks between September and February, from the surface of Mars to the history of the telescope.

news.title: Thank you to everyone who came to the meteor watch
news.text: We counted over two hundred meteors, and one cloud.

news.title: The society telescope has been repaired
news.text: The mount has a new motor and the finder scope has been aligned for the first time in years.

news.title: A new observing field
news.text: We now have permission to observe from the field behind the library, away from the street lights.

join: We are about thirty members, with telescopes ranging from a pair of binoculars to something the size of a washing machine.
Come to any meeting. If the sky is clear we will show you the Moon, Jupiter or whatever else is up.

faq.a: No. Members are happy to share theirs, and the society owns one you can borrow.

faq.q: What should I wear for an observing night?
faq.a: More than you think. Hat, gloves and a flask.
We have a talk indoors, and sometimes the cloud goes away at ten o'clock.
